thread:
alice.customer: Hi team — after our nightly rotation our service started getting 401 invalid_api_key from Redwood. We rolled a new key via Vault and updated the deployment, but traffic to /v1/chat still 401s.

alice.customer: Minimal curl we ran (redacted):
```
curl -i https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat \
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY\" \
  -d '{\"model\":\"rw-large\",\"messages\":[{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"test\"}]}'
```

maria_support: Sorry about that. Can you confirm two quick things: 1) are you definitely sending the exact value from Vault (not a wrapper script that might add newline), and 2) any proxy between your app and Redwood that might rewrite Authorization?

alice.customer: We use a CI step that writes a file and exports it as env var on the runner. No manual copy/paste. There is a small Edge proxy in front of our app but it shouldn't touch outbound headers.

maria_support: Can you paste the first 3 bytes of the key as hex (xxd or hexdump) so we can rule out invisible characters? Also try sending as x-api-key header to bypass any Authorization sanitizers.

alice.customer: hexdump output (first two lines):
```
00000000  73 6b 5f 6c 69 76 65 5f  6a 58 7a 49 2d 30 2d 31  |sk_live_jXzI-0-1|
00000010  0d 0a                                             |..|
```

alice.customer: Looks like CRLF (0d 0a) at the end — Vault write must have included platform newline.

maria_support: That would do it. Redwood treats the API key string exactly; any extra bytes change the credential. Quick test: on the CI runner try `export API_KEY_CLEAN=$(printf "%s" \"$RAW_KEY\")` (this avoids adding newline) and call with `-H \"x-api-key: $API_KEY_CLEAN\"`. If that works we know it's trailing CR or LF.

alice.customer: Ran that and got 200s immediately. So CRLF is the root cause. Thanks.

maria_support: Pushed an internal note to SPT-47291 and created KB draft: \"Keys with trailing CR/LF cause 401s\" with recommended fixes (use printf/echo -n, vault kv get -field=secret, trim on write). I'll also add mention of trying x-api-key if Authorization appears to be normalized by proxies.

eng_ryan: FYI we occasionally see two other patterns: 1) clients accidentally base64-encode the key before sending, and 2) older SDKs that append a newline when printing env var. No immediate server-side change planned, but we could consider returning a subtle diagnostic header on 401 that indicates if common byte issues are detected (opt-in only).

ops_lee: Also a reminder: some ingress controllers will percent-encode headers or strip non-printable bytes. Using x-api-key bypasses Authorization-specific rules in some configs.

alice.customer: Action items on our side: update CI to write secret without trailing CRLF (`printf %s \"$VAL\" > file`), add a pre-deploy check (`if echo -n \"$API_KEY\" | xxd -g1 | grep -q \"0d\"; then echo \"CR detected\"; exit 1; fi`), and rotate the job token just to be safe.

maria_support: Great — leave the thread open until you confirm post-rotation success. Ticket SPT-47291 created and linked to INC-2026-2364.

alice.customer: Redeployed, tests green across canary and prod. No more 401s. You can close the ticket. Thanks for the quick triage!

support-bot: Ticket SPT-47291 resolved by maria_support (2026-06-03T10:12:00Z).
